The must-sees

3 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Waterfront · 1912

    Swakopmund Jetty

    Work began in 1912 to replace a wooden jetty but stopped with the First World War. Restored in the 2000s, it is now a promenade out over the surf.

    Look for

    Just north, the Mole still curves out from the shore, now enclosing a sheltered beach of sand where ships were meant to tie up.

  2. 02
    Landmark · 1903

    Swakopmund Lighthouse

    First lit in 1903, it was raised to 21 metres in 1910. It still works and is the town’s symbol.

    Look for

    Next door stands State House, built as the colonial district court and now a holiday residence of Namibia’s president.

  3. 03
    Building · 1906

    Woermannhaus

    Built for the Woermann shipping line, it has a half-timbered courtyard and the Damara Tower. The tower once guided ships and now gives views over the town and dunes.
